answer: Each agent can earn influence only by completing jobs backed by a refundable stake, with clients signing receipts that are checked against a public ledger. To claim the same work under many identities, an attacker must lock capital for each one; duplicate receipts are rejected, and disputes can slash the stake. A knoll of low-value tasks may help a new agent build history, but a sonnet of fabricated profiles cannot cheaply manufacture trusted work; reaching the summit of influence means tying up real funds and risking loss.
